newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Far East Gold - Trade bullish on year-end prospects.
newsitem.headline: Far East Gold - Trade bullish on year-end prospects.

text.p: Asian gold traders were mildly bullish on the year-end prospects for gold based on spritely physical demand but said on Friday that recent options plays had kept spot prices range-bound.
"Prices are looking steady to firmer. There's steady demand all around the region although it's not spectacular," a Singapore bank trader said.
A senior Hong Kong gold trader said much of Asia's demand was fuelled by India while Taiwan, China and Hong Kong had been disappointing.

Taiwan's gold demand fell steadily after the first quarter's buying boom triggered by China-Taiwan political tensions, the trader said. Taiwan's gold imports plunged 31.04 percent to 6.064 tonnes in October from 8.794 tonnes a year earlier.
Compared to 1994, Chinese gold demand this year was weak due to the country's economic slowdown, while Hong Kong's booming equity markets were a detrimental distraction for gold, the source said.
India's gold demand, although weak during the Diwali festival in November, was healthy overall after a good harvest and with the marriage season coming up, the source said.
One gold jeweller in Singapore said demand had improved over the last two months.
"You should see the price of gold climbing slightly as retail sales recover," the jeweller said.
Much of Indian gold imports are channelled through Singapore and Dubai.

Singapore traders said producer selling would hit the market if gold poked its way above US$384 an ounce. Japanese trying to take advantage of fluctuations in the dollar/yen could also spark gold sales, they said.
"You'll see the sellers come out if we hit $384 to $385 an ounce. The key support lies around $377 but the range at the moment is between $381 and $385," a bank dealer said.
Singapore gold premiums were quoted steady in a range between 35 and 45 U.S. cents an ounce.
"The premiums are just holding at their current levels. The market is in a rough equilibrium," one trader said.
Relatively hectic options activity had kept gold within claustrophobic ranges, traders said.
"Volatilities are so low that it's quite a cheap game for funds to play," said one gold trader.
One-month volatilities were up about 0.7 percent to 5.1 percent, while three-month were also at about 5.1 percent, up 0.5 percent, an options trader said.

"What players are doing in November is they're bidding up volatilities and saying 'I'll buy a volatility at a higher level' because they want to buy low and sell high and take advantage of moving markets," the trader said.
"If you buy an option, you get positive gamma, and you buy low and sell high. You want gold to move, so you're long volatility or short volatility," he said.
